target_claim: In the stated zero-exponent case, the function φ(x)=x^(q/p) is well-defined as a real function and can be used in Jensen's inequality.
source_quote:
0042 | Consider the [[Definition:Real Function|function]] $\phi: \R_{\ge 0} \to \R_{\ge 0}$ defined as:
0043 | :$\forall x \in \R_{\ge 0}: \map \phi x = x^{q/p}$
